assessment: The observed fulfillment rate is 22/30, below 90%; two of four closing comparisons exceed one item. Neither missing stock nor insufficient type variety is established. Search location and the interval between counts leave distinct uncertainties.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: visible table-level availability signs could make equipment already outside cabinets discoverable, effectively treating occupied tables as temporary pickup points for unused equipment.
openings.delta: Add folded paper signs with full type names and separate 'available here' and 'in use' counts. Participants update their table's sign when equipment arrives, leaves, or becomes available. Keep cabinet storage and permanent asset numbers; use removable duplicate number labels where needed for reading.
openings.prediction: Requests involving equipment outside cabinets should become faster if visibility is limiting; stale signs or predominantly cabinet-based delays would weaken this mechanism.
openings.probe: First time cabinet search and table search separately. Pilot signs at existing tables, recording sign accuracy and request duration across four sessions. Compare closing sign totals plus cabinet totals with the physical count. Record preparation time and spending, stopping preparation at 120 minutes or 60 units.
assumptions: Signs fit on existing tables without obstructing work.
Participants can maintain anonymous aggregate counts with little effort.
Visible unused equipment can be collected without interrupting its table.

openings.claim: Do closing discrepancies reflect counting error, or equipment movement during the interval before morning verification?
openings.delta: Separate the accuracy of a closing count from the stability of inventory between two measurement times.
openings.prediction: Agreement with an immediate physical verification but disagreement next morning would favor interval movement; immediate disagreement would implicate counting or concurrent movement.
openings.probe: For four closings, retain the routine count and immediately verify physical items by permanent number. Record any movement during verification and request an anonymous numbered movement slip for later transfers. Mark unobserved intervals inconclusive; compare signed discrepancies and movement records. Use stationery within the shared preparation cap.
assumptions: The steward has time for verification without interrupting workshops.
Later movements can be recorded sufficiently completely to distinguish explanations.
